chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Al-Washa', who said:

I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a man who buys from a man a dry, known land for one hundred kurrs, on the condition that he gives him the produce from the land. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is prohibited.' I said to him: 'What do you say, may Allah make me your ransom, if he buys from him the land with a known measure and wheat from other than it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.أَرْضاً جُرْبَاناً: Dry land (land not yet cultivated or producing)
key_terms.مِائَةِ كُرٍّ: One hundred kurrs (a unit of volume measurement)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between prohibited and permissible land rent in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the prohibition of *ju'lah* (renting land for a fixed quantity of its own produce) due to the uncertainty (*gharar*) of the yield, while permitting rent for a known quantity of an external commodity like wheat. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on minimizing risk in contracts, a principle rooted in the Prophetic tradition of avoiding *jahala* (ignorance/uncertainty) in trade.
